objectives.understand: The four parts that make an agent different from a chatbot: instructions, memory, tools and a trigger.
objectives.do: Turn your Playbook into a persona block so every new chat starts already briefed.
objectives.demonstrate: Identify the four parts in a real setup and know what a briefed chat can and cannot do.
objectives.apply: Run one real work request with your persona in place and compare it with an unbriefed chat.

discover.title: Mission briefing: the assistant who remembers
discover.scenario: Every morning Fatima, who runs a pharmacy in Kaduna, types the same thing: 'I run a pharmacy, use a warm tone, never mention prices I haven't confirmed…' Imagine an assistant that already knows all of that before she types a word. That is the difference between a chatbot and an agent, and you have been building one all week.

keyIdeas: An agent = standing instructions + memory + tools + a trigger.
Your Playbook is the beginning of a harness: the scaffolding that holds it together.
A briefed chat drafts better, but it hasn't read your stock, sent a message or booked anything. You stay responsible.

missions.title: Find the four parts
missions.scenario: Fatima's setup for weekly restock reminders.
missions.prompt: Sort each piece into the agent part it is.

items.text: 'You are my pharmacy assistant. Warm tone. Never state a price I haven't confirmed.'
items.feedback: Role and rules, stated once: standing instructions.

items.text: Her list of regular suppliers and the reorder template from her Playbook
items.feedback: Context and templates the assistant carries: memory.

items.text: The stock spreadsheet she pastes in each week
items.feedback: Material the assistant may use: tools.

items.text: A phone reminder every Monday at 8am
items.feedback: When the work happens: the trigger.

missions.hint: Instructions = how to behave. Memory = what it knows about you. Tools = what it may use. Trigger = when it runs.
missions.support: Compare it to briefing a new staff member: the rules you give them, the files they keep, the equipment they use, and their start time.
missions.explain: Those four parts are all an agent is. Fatima's version is built from free features and her own notes, and it already behaves differently from a blank chat.

missions.title: Who did what?
missions.scenario: With the persona in place, the AI drafted: 'We have blue pens in stock; collection from the shop only.' A customer asks if you'll send the message.

options.text: The AI checked the shop's stock before writing.
options.feedback: No. It only knows what you pasted. It never saw your inventory.

options.text: The AI drafted the reply from the context you gave it. You check the stock and send it yourself.
options.feedback: Correct. You supplied the context and you remain responsible for the action.

options.text: The message has already been sent to the customer.
options.feedback: No. A briefed chat drafts; it doesn't send messages for you.

options.text: The AI will now remember your stock levels automatically.
options.feedback: No. Stock changes. You paste current facts each time.

missions.hint: Think about what the chat can actually see and do.
missions.support: The chat only sees the words in the conversation. It can't open your shelves, your phone contacts or your inventory.
missions.explain: Being honest about the limits is what keeps you safe: the agent drafts, you verify and act.

advanced.title: Advanced: tighten the persona block
advanced.scenario: Your draft persona says only: 'You are my assistant. Be helpful.'
advanced.prompt: Which additions turn it into a real briefing? Select all that apply.

options.text: My role: admin officer in a state ministry.
options.feedback: Yes. Role sets vocabulary and judgement.

options.text: My rules: never paste confidential material; always flag facts I must verify.
options.feedback: Yes. Rules carry your privacy and verification habits into every chat.

options.text: My formats: memos in my ministry format; reports with action points and owners.
options.feedback: Yes. Formats mean you never re-explain the shape.

options.text: Ask me one clarifying question if my request is genuinely unclear.
options.feedback: Yes. This stops it guessing when it shouldn't.
No. You want an assistant that flags problems, not one that flatters.

advanced.hint: The lesson's persona block has role, rules, formats and one behaviour instruction.
advanced.support: Look for the parts that tell it who you are, what it must never do, what shape to produce, and when to ask.
advanced.explain: Role, rules, formats and a clarifying-question rule make up the persona block from today. 'Always agree' makes an assistant less useful and less safe.
